languageAdaptation.japaneseConcept: plain, polite and honorific register by listener

lessons.sourceEnglishObjective: Deliver the same news to a crew member, a homeowner, your manager and an inspector in the right register
lessons.sourceEnglishSpeaking: You are the crew lead and the AI will play the people you work with, one after another: tell each of them that you found rotten deck, switching between tú and usted and using softeners like quisiera and me gustaría.
lessons.title: 相手に合わせた日本語の話し方
lessons.objective: 同じ野地板の損傷を作業員、家主、上司、検査員に適切な話し方で伝える。
lessons.focus: 普通体 and です・ます体 change register. お／ご～する and ～ていただけますか make a customer or inspector request polite; titles such as さん and 様 are chosen by relationship.

cards.en: to speak in the plain form
polite address for a customer or colleague

cards.ja: 名前に「さん」や「様」を付ける
cards.en: to attach a respectful suffix to a name
cards.sourceEnglish: respectful title before a first name

cards.ja: 見て、腐朽した木材が見つかった。
お忙しいところ失礼します、○○様。
cards.en: Excuse me for interrupting you, Ms. or Mr. [name].

cards.ja: 見つかった箇所についてお伝えしたいことがあります。
cards.en: I would like to tell you about something we found.
cards.sourceEnglish: I'd like to mention something we found.

cards.ja: その箇所をお見せしてもよろしいでしょうか。
cards.en: May I show you the area?
cards.sourceEnglish: Would you allow me to show you the area?

cards.ja: 野地板に問題が見つかりましたので、ご報告します。
cards.en: I am reporting that we found a problem in the roof deck.
cards.sourceEnglish: I'm letting you know that we found a problem.

cards.ja: 覆う前にご確認いただけますか。
cards.en: Could you inspect it before we cover it?
cards.sourceEnglish: I'd like you to check it.

cards.ja: どのようにお呼びすればよいでしょうか。
cards.en: How would you like me to address you?
cards.sourceEnglish: Should I address you as usted or tú?

cards.en: You can use -san with my name.
cards.sourceEnglish: Use tú with me, no problem.

reader.ja: ケビンは現場で相手ごとにどう話せばよいか知りたくて、ロヘリオに尋ねます。
reader.en: Kevin asks Rogelio how to speak to different people at the job site.
reader.sourceEnglish: Kevin wants to know how to talk to each person on the job, and Rogelio explains it to him with an example.

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「用件は同じです。腐朽した木材が見つかりました。ただし、相手に合わせて話し方を変えます。」
reader.en: Rogelio: The news is the same: we found rotten wood. The tone changes with the listener.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: The message is the same, we found rotten wood, but the tone changes depending on the person.

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「親しい作業仲間には普通体も使いますが、失礼な言い方はしません。」
reader.en: Rogelio: With a close crew member, plain speech may fit, but rude wording does not.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: With the crew we use tú, sometimes a nickname, but never anything rude.

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「作業仲間には『見て、腐朽した木材が見つかった。上がってきたら見せるよ』と言えます。」
reader.en: Rogelio: To a crew member I can say, 'Look, we found rotten wood. Come up and I'll show you.'
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: To the crew I say: Look, we found rotten wood; come up and I'll show you.

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「家主には丁寧語を使い、名前が分かれば『○○様』と呼びます。」
reader.en: Rogelio: With the homeowner, use polite Japanese and an appropriate name and title.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: With the homeowner I use usted and a title, señora or doña Carmen; with her husband, señor.

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「『お忙しいところ失礼します。見つかった箇所についてお伝えしたいことがあります』と言います。」
reader.en: Rogelio: I say, 'Excuse the interruption. I would like to tell you about something we found.'
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: To her I say: Sorry to bother you, ma'am; I'd like to mention something we found.

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「そして『その箇所をお見せしてもよろしいでしょうか』と尋ねます。」
reader.en: Rogelio: Then I ask, 'May I show you the area?'
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: And then I ask her: Would you allow me to show you the area?

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「上司にも丁寧に話しますが、要点を先に伝えます。」
reader.en: Rogelio: I also speak politely to the manager, but lead with the point.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: With the company manager I also use usted, but I go straight to the point.

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「『野地板に問題が見つかりましたので、ご報告します。写真を今送ります』と伝えます。」
reader.en: Rogelio: 'I am reporting a problem in the roof deck. I am sending the photos now.'
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: I'm letting you know that we found a problem in the deck, and I'm sending you the photos now.

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「検査員には、くだけた言葉や冗談を避け、さらに改まった言い方をします。」
reader.en: Rogelio: With the inspector, avoid slang and jokes and use a more formal tone.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: With the inspector there's more formality: no slang and no jokes.

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「『覆う前にご確認いただけますか』と依頼します。」
reader.en: Rogelio: I ask, 'Could you inspect it before we cover it?'
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: To him I would say: I'd like you to check it before we cover it.

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「『お見せします』『ご確認いただけますか』は、丁寧な説明や依頼に使えます。」
reader.en: Rogelio: 'I will show you' and 'Could you inspect it?' are polite ways to explain and ask.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Quisiera, me gustaría and podría are words that soften a request.

reader.ja: ケビン「エルネストさんのような年上の作業員には、どう話しますか。」
reader.en: Kevin: How should I speak to an older crew member such as Ernesto?
reader.sourceEnglish: Kevin: And what if someone on the crew is older, like Don Ernesto?

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「まず『どのようにお呼びすればよいでしょうか』と丁寧に尋ねます。」
reader.en: Rogelio: First ask politely, 'How would you like me to address you?'
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Then ask him politely: Should I address you as usted or tú?

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「『さんで大丈夫です』と言う人もいます。」
reader.en: Rogelio: Some people will say, 'Using -san is fine.'
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Many will tell you: Use tú with me, no problem.

reader.ja: ロヘリオ「迷ったら丁寧な言い方から始めて、相手の希望に合わせます。」
reader.en: Rogelio: When unsure, begin politely and adjust to the person's preference.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: But if you're not sure, start with usted, because nobody gets offended by respect.

forms.exampleJa: 相手に合わせて丁寧に話します。
forms.exampleEn: We speak politely according to the listener.

sourceEnglish.exampleEnglish: Should I address you as usted or tú?

forms.exampleJa: ケビンは相手ごとの話し方を知りたいと思っています。
forms.exampleEn: Kevin wants to know how to speak to each person.

sourceEnglish.exampleEnglish: Kevin wants to know how to talk to each person.

forms.exampleJa: その箇所をお見せしてもよろしいでしょうか。
forms.exampleEn: May I show you the area?

sourceEnglish.exampleEnglish: Would you allow me to show you the area?

forms.exampleJa: ロヘリオは上司に写真を見せます。
forms.exampleEn: Rogelio shows the photos to the manager.

sourceEnglish.exampleEnglish: Rogelio shows the photos to the manager.

forms.exampleJa: 用件は同じでも、相手によって話し方は変わります。
forms.exampleEn: The message stays the same, but the tone changes with the listener.

sourceEnglish.exampleEnglish: The message is the same, but the tone changes depending on the person.

speaking.opening: 同じ野地板の損傷でも、作業仲間、家主、上司、検査員にはそれぞれ適切な話し方で伝えます。
speaking.goalEn: Tell a crew member, homeowner, manager, and inspector about the same deck problem in appropriate Japanese register.

modes.see: Match each listener with an appropriate Japanese form of address.
modes.recall: Recall plain form, polite form, name suffixes, and formal requests.
modes.hear: Distinguish 見せる from お見せする when spoken.
modes.type: Type 'May I show you the area?' in polite Japanese.
modes.say: Report the same rotten-deck finding to four listeners in appropriate register.
modes.write: Write a crew version and an inspector version of the same message.
